why: Team C loses its own hue and renders as the white fallback -- the state that shipped between issue #281's descriptor landing and TEAM_COLORS gaining a third entry. It is not a crash and not a blank: `teamColor` still returns a colour, the ring still draws, the shell still tints, the tread trail still blends, and the stock chip still paints. What is lost is that a 2v1v1 match renders one whole SIDE in the fallback white, which the player has no way to read as a team. Deliberately mutated to `0xffffff` -- the actual fallback -- rather than to a duplicate of team A or B: a duplicate is caught by the pairwise-distinctness sweep, which makes that the easy half, while the fallback is a DISTINCT colour and passes every distinctness assertion. It is caught instead by the stock-readout case that asserts team 2's chip is TEAM_COLORS[2] and is not the fallback, which is the one place the two are told apart. Scoped to entities.test.ts and hud.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. RE-ANCHORED for issue #579, which re-picked team B from #3b82ff to #fcc0fc: this entry names the whole TEAM_COLORS line, so the colour change turned it into FAILED-TO-APPLY -- a guard that stopped guarding, reported by the sweep and by nothing else. That is now the third entry in one session killed by a value it was anchored on (see `quad-board-loses-its-mirror-symmetry` and the two egress killedBy moves), which is an argument for anchoring on the SHAPE of a line rather than its contents wherever a mutation can express itself that way.

killedBy: player identity: ring and shell tint TEAM_COLORS: exactly 3 hues, measurably clear of each other, the player hull and the placeholder
why: Restores the blue team B that issue #579 replaced. It is unequal to every other colour in the game, so the byte-inequality sweep this entry's test replaced passed on it -- and it sits 2.09 from the player's default hull #3d7bd6 once composited, which is a blue ring drawn around a blue tank. That is the whole case for measuring instead of comparing: the defect and the assertion that was supposed to catch it coexisted happily. Filed in presentation.json because its file is src/presentation/identity.ts -- `validateManifest`'s one-file-per-area rule (issue #505) requires it, and caught this entry filed under render.json.

Stops the counter-rotation, so the marker spins with the hull again -- which is what it did before issue #630 noticed, and is invisible for the circular annulus that shipped. It is fatal for BOTH candidates: slots 3 and 4 of the shape style are the same 4-gon 45 degrees apart, so a spinning marker makes the square and the diamond one marker wearing two names for most of every match. The failure mode this guards is specifically NOT a crash or a blank screen -- it is a marker that looks fine in a still and is unreadable in play, which no unit assertion on geometry alone can see. Killed by the holds-a-marker-vertex-at-a-fixed-world-position case, which composes the real parent/child matrices at seven body angles rather than trusting the sign; its negative control proves the same case fails when the counter-rotation is absent, so this entry cannot be killed by an accidentally symmetric marker.

The OTHER way to get the counter-rotation wrong, and the reason the derivation is written out in the function's own comment. A flipped sign does not hold the marker still and does not leave it alone: it spins it at DOUBLE rate. At small turn rates that reads as wobble rather than as a bug, which is exactly how a wrong sign survives a look-at-it review. Filed separately from the returns-zero entry above because the two are different mistakes with different symptoms, and an assertion that caught only one of them would leave the likelier one uncovered.
